findings.title: Exit code 4 silently changes meaning from 'recreate required' to 'feature disabled'
findings.body: This change reassigns the `check` command's exit codes: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` moves from 4 to 3, and 4 becomes `FEATURE_DISABLED`. The tool's own documentation (update-compatibility.adoc) explicitly tells consumers to rely only on the exit code for automation, so exit codes are the public contract of this command. Any pipeline written against the previously released behavior (exit 4 = rolling upgrade not possible, shut down the deployment) will now either misinterpret 'feature disabled' as 'recreate required' (causing unnecessary downtime) or, worse, fail to handle the new exit code 3 and potentially treat a required recreate upgrade as an error or even proceed with a rolling upgrade against an incompatible Infinispan/Keycloak version. Even for a preview feature, reusing a previously emitted exit code for a different meaning is risky; a safer approach would be to keep 4 as recreate and use a new, previously unused code (e.g., 5) for the feature-disabled case, or at minimum call out the renumbering explicitly in the docs/release notes.

findings.title: CAUTION claims the Operator will fail without the rolling-updates feature, contradicting the documented default behavior
findings.body: The new CAUTION block states: 'While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail.' This contradicts the rest of the same section, which documents that with `update.strategy` unset the operator 'defaults to mimicking Keycloak 26.1 or older behavior' (scale down on image change, rolling for config changes) — behavior that does not require the feature. The updated `UpgradeTest` confirms this: `createInitialDeployment` with a `null` strategy deliberately does not enable the `rolling-updates` feature and the deployment/upgrade proceeds normally. As written, the warning tells users the operator will break unless they enable the feature, which will drive them to enable a preview feature unnecessarily (or panic when they don't). The caution should be scoped to 'when configuring `spec.update.strategy`' rather than claiming the operator fails outright.

findings.title: New exit codes 3 and 4 are never asserted in tests
findings.body: The docs for the update-compatibility tool explicitly instruct users to 'rely only on the exit code of the check command' for automation, making the exit codes the tool's stable contract. However, none of the tests verify the new codes: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error message (never that the process exits with code 4 / `CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED`), and `testWrongVersions` only asserts error messages (never that a recreate-incompatible result exits with code 3). Only the success path asserts `exitCode() == 0`. A regression that swapped or dropped these exit codes would break consumer automation without failing any test; assertions on the exit codes for both the feature-disabled and recreate-required paths should be added.
